answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it may place orders or earn reputation. If several linked identities collude, they must fund each one separately; detected double-spending or coordinated fraud burns the bonds, while honest history accrues slowly and cannot be copied to a fresh account. A nebula of cheap aliases then becomes an expensive orchard to maintain: the attacker ties up capital and risks losing it, rather than gaining influence by merely repeating a fable about being many users.
